frozen_decisions_applied: Plan #2, verbatim: 'Introduce a ProvisioningSecretProvider port: production adapter reads per-device manufacturing proof-of-possession material; development adapter may generate and print a one-time secret; production startup fails closed when material is absent.' -- implemented exactly: production reads manufacturing_provisioning_get_proof_of_possession() (S5) and returns kUnavailable (never falls back) on any non-available status; development draws 128 bits of fresh randomness every call and logs it via ESP_LOGI.

Plan #3, verbatim: 'Commissioning mode starts only after first-boot policy or trusted physical button action and expires according to ZGW_COMMISSIONING_WINDOW_SECONDS; approved default is 600 seconds and every production value must remain inside FD-13.' -- implemented as an explicit-time state machine consuming security_bounds().commissioning_window_seconds (S6 slice 1); first-boot policy trigger implemented verbatim from the plan's own Migration/compatibility text ('Upgrade boots into restricted migration mode if no admin credential exists'); trusted-physical-button-action trigger has no button-driver plumbing to call it yet (see deviations).

Plan #5, verbatim: 'Enrollment creates a PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 admin password verifier with a per-device random 128-bit salt. Calibrate iterations to 250-500 ms on ESP32-C6 with a hard minimum of 50,000; store the selected iteration count with the verifier. Never store or log plaintext password.' -- implemented exactly: 128-bit salt from hal_random_fill_bytes(); calibrate_pbkdf2_iterations() targets [250,500]ms with a hard 50,000 floor never violated regardless of measured device speed; iteration count stored alongside salt+hash in the fixed-layout AdminVerifierRecord; the password itself is never stored, logged, or retained beyond the stack of create_admin_verifier()/verify_admin_password().

FD-22 'platform-first, security-equivalent implementation': production PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 uses the real mbedtls_pkcs5_pbkdf2_hmac_ext(); the host-only self-contained SHA-256/HMAC-SHA256/PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 fallback is justified by a documented unmet product requirement (zero crypto library dev headers on zgw-host-tools:s0, confirmed by direct recon, no Dockerfile in this repository to rebuild that image) and is never compiled into a production build -- mirrors hal_random.c's already-established ESP_PLATFORM-vs-host split.

production_profile_kconfig_gap_closed.detail: Recon confirmed CONFIG_ZGW_PRODUCTION_BUILD is a build-time-only CMake environment variable (selects which sdkconfig.defaults* files get layered) that never becomes a compiled CONFIG_ZGW_* macro -- no existing symbol let application code distinguish 'this is a production build' at runtime. New ZGW_PRODUCTION_PROFILE Kconfig bool (default n) closes the gap: declared in main/Kconfig.projbuild, set to y only in sdkconfig.production.esp32c6, and enforced by verify_production_security_profile.py's REQUIRED_SYMBOLS (a production build omitting it now fails verification). Confirmed end-to-end against a real generated sdkconfig from a ZGW_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1 idf.py build: CONFIG_ZGW_PRODUCTION_PROFILE=y actually appears, and verify_production_security_profile.py against that real file reports OK.

hal_time_implemented.detail: hal_time_now_ms() wraps the real esp_timer_get_time() on ESP_PLATFORM (confirmed signature via grep inside espressif/idf:release-v5.5 before writing any code) and POSIX clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, ...) on host. Consumed by both commissioning_window.cpp (expiry) and admin_verifier.cpp (calibration timing).

admin_verifier_implemented.detail: AdminVerifierRecord (16-byte salt + 32-byte hash + 4-byte iteration count) with explicit serialize/deserialize (never reinterpret_cast, matching persisted_device_state.hpp's convention), stored under NvsNamespaceId::kAdminVerifier's 'admin_verifier' key (encryption_required=true). create_admin_verifier() draws a fresh 128-bit salt, calibrates iterations (50,000 hard floor, targets 250-500ms, bounded 6-attempt proportional scaling), derives the hash. verify_admin_password() re-derives and compares in constant time, and rejects any record whose stored iteration count is below the hard minimum outright (never trusts a tampered/corrupt record to gate its own cost).

host_crypto_backend_implemented_and_vali.detail: zgw-host-tools:s0 has zero crypto library dev headers (confirmed: no mbedtls anywhere; OpenSSL runtime .so present but no dev headers/libssl-dev; no Dockerfile in this repository to rebuild the image). A self-contained SHA-256/HMAC-SHA256/PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 implementation, private to admin_verifier.cpp's host (#else ESP_PLATFORM) branch, was written and independently validated via scratch files BEFORE being integrated: SHA-256 matched Python hashlib.sha256() byte-for-byte across empty/short/multi-chunk (>55-byte) inputs; HMAC-SHA256 matched Python hmac.new(key, msg, hashlib.sha256) (one test-harness mistake caught and fixed here -- a hardcoded message length off by one byte, not a real algorithm bug); PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 matched Python hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', ...) for 1-round, 4096-round, and a second-password vector. Never compiled into a production (ESP_PLATFORM) build.

provisioning_secret_provider_implemented.detail: provisioning_secret_provider_get() switches on CONFIG_ZGW_PRODUCTION_PROFILE (defined(ESP_PLATFORM) && defined(...) && value, matching this repository's established guarded-macro precedent, e.g. hal_rcp_uart_backend.c/ota_manifest.cpp). Production reads manufacturing_provisioning_get_proof_of_possession() (S5's tls_provisioning_storage_port.hpp) and fails closed (kUnavailable, never a fallback) on any non-available status. Development draws 128 bits of fresh randomness every call (never persisted) and logs it via ESP_LOGI, mirroring main/app_main.cpp's existing Wi-Fi AP passphrase delivery posture for the identical no-display/UART-only reason. Nothing calls this function yet -- the real enrollment consumer is a later S6 sub-slice, matching tls_provisioning_storage_port.hpp's own established 'port ahead of its pipeline' precedent.

commissioning_window_implemented.detail: CommissioningWindowState{active, started_at_ms, trigger} plus start/is_active/stop, all taking now_ms explicitly (mirrors security_bounds()'s pure-accessor testability discipline -- host tests control elapsed time deterministically). Expiry compares against security_bounds().commissioning_window_seconds * 1000 (S6 slice 1). commissioning_window_first_boot_policy_applies() implements the plan's own Migration/compatibility text verbatim, built on admin_verifier.hpp's admin_credential_exists(). Neither the trusted-physical-button-action trigger (no button-driver plumbing exists in this repository) nor any actual gating of request-handling behavior on commissioning_window_is_active() is implemented -- this sub-slice is the window's own state machine only.
